title: Exploring the Nature, History, and Culture of Kalimantan with WikiBanua
content: WikiBanua is a documentation project focused on cultural heritage sites, landmarks, natural landscapes, and public facilities across Kalimantan. Following its successful implementation in various locations throughout South Kalimantan—supported by a grant from Wikimedia Indonesia through the “Dana Wiki” program—WikiBanua expanded its reach into neighboring provinces, Central Kalimantan and East Kalimantan, under the initiatives “WikiBanua 3.0” and “WikiBanua 4.0.” Unlike previous iterations, this phase of WikiBanua was managed by a two-person team: Ilham Mufti Laksono (User:Ilham Mufti Laksono) as Project Manager and Arief Rahman (User:Ezagren) as Assistant Project Manager, both of whom are members of the Wikimedia Banjar Community. Nevertheless, the project proved successful thanks to the involvement of local volunteers and contributors to Wikimedia projects across South, Central, and East Kalimantan, who participated in a range of WikiBanua activities, including documentation efforts, workshops, and in-person meetups.

title: From Documenting Local Vocabulary to Organizing Wikipedia Contests: Two Workshops at WikiCamp Morocco 2026
content:
From 18 to 21 October 2026, Wikimedia Morocco organized the fourth edition of WikiCamp Morocco in Marrakesh under the theme “From Contribution to Initiative: Building a Team of Organizers Together.”

The event brought together Wikimedia contributors from 16 Moroccan cities, with a programme focused on developing organizational skills, sharing technical knowledge, and preparing volunteers to lead Wikimedia activities in their communities.

During the camp, I facilitated two workshops addressing different aspects of Wikimedia participation: documenting Moroccan vocabulary and pronunciation using Lingua Libre, and organizing Wikipedia editing contests, from selecting articles to preparing and managing contest pages.

The first workshop, titled “A Word from My City” (كلمة من مدينتي), focused on documenting regional vocabulary in Moroccan Darija, including the pronunciation, meaning, and geographical usage of words and expressions.

Moroccan Darija varies considerably across regions. Some words are widely used in one city but rarely heard elsewhere, while others have different pronunciations or meanings depending on the speaker’s location.

title: From Figma to a Working Prototype: Building Wikimedia Morocco’s Website with OFPPT Students in Two Days
content:
On 22–23 October 2026, 20 students from Morocco’s Office of Vocational Training and Employment Promotion (OFPPT) joined Wikimedia Morocco contributors at ISTA Taddart in Agadir for a two-day Mini-Hackathon. Participants were divided into four teams, each working on a technical project related to Wikimedia.

I mentored a team of five students responsible for developing a prototype of Wikimedia Morocco’s official website. Our objective was to build a platform that could present the user group’s activities, projects, and resources while providing a maintainable foundation for future development.

Rather than focusing exclusively on delivering a set of web pages, we approached the hackathon as a complete software development exercise, covering requirements analysis, interface design, implementation, integration, testing, and project presentation.

We began on 22 October by identifying the website’s main requirements and defining its core structure.

Our priorities were to organize information clearly, improve access to Wikimedia Morocco’s activities and resources, and provide a responsive experience across desktop and mobile devices.

title: When Heritage Connects Communities
content:
What happens when Wikimedia communities from India and Ukraine come together to explore and collect each other’s heritage? Heritage Across Borders turned this idea into a diverse and multilingual campaign, bringing contributors together from 15 to 24 August 2026, around both countries’ Independence Days.

The core objective was simple: discover another culture, document its heritage on wiki, and make that knowledge available in more languages. To make this objective a reality, Wikimedians from India worked on documenting Ukrainian heritage, while the Ukrainian community contributed to articles about Indian cultural heritage.

  • 833 articles created
  • 33 articles improved
  • Ukrainian, Hindi, Malayalam, Kannada, Tulu, Punjabi, Assamese, Tamil and Telugu

title: What’s new in The Wikipedia Library? (July – September 2026)
content:
Over the past three months, we secured access to two new resources for eligible editors: The Chronicle of Higher Education and Datawrapper. We also raised awareness of the library through community convenings across the globe.

The Chronicle of Higher Education, a leading resource for independent journalism, career development, and academic analysis, made 100 subscriptions available for Wikipedia Library users (apply here). Thanks to an introduction by Doc James, Datawrapper is offering 100 free accounts for editors to create charts, maps, and tables for Wikimedia projects (apply here).

Adam Matthew Digital is transitioning to the Library Bundle, granting instant access to all eligible editors. Springer Nature has renewed access through the Library Bundle and E-Yearbook has also been renewed for another year (apply here).

title: Beyond Edit-a-Thons: Building Sustainable Pathways for Queer Wikimedia Contributors
content:
What happens after the event ends? Reflections from Queering Wiki 2026 on strengthening Wikimedia communities and sustaining participation.

Wikimedia communities know how to bring people into the room. Edit-a-thons, workshops, and campaigns introduce people to free knowledge, help them develop skills, and create opportunities to connect with others. But what happens when the event ends?

Some participants may want to continue contributing but need guidance, resources, or opportunities to collaborate. Others may be ready to take on new responsibilities but not know where to begin. Without pathways to continued participation, the momentum created by an event can be difficult to sustain.

This question shaped my presentation, “Beyond Edit-a-Thons: Building Sustainable Pathways for Queer Wikimedia Contributors,” at the Queering Wiki Conference 2026 in Montréal, Canada. Drawing on the work of the EduWiki Hub, I explored how mentorship, peer learning, shared resources, and community support can contribute to more sustainable participation.

An event can introduce someone to Wikimedia, but attendance alone does not tell us whether they feel connected, supported, or able to continue contributing.
snippet: What happens after the event ends? Reflections from Queering Wiki 2026 on strengthening Wikimedia communities and sustaining participation.
creator: Bukola James

title: The Virtual Room: How Volunteers Brought Wikimania Paris to the World
content:
From 22 to 25 July 2026, Wikimania Paris featured a room that nobody could physically walk into.

The Virtual Room was a dedicated digital space built exclusively for online attendees, complete with its own dedicated programming and unique content unavailable anywhere else at the venue.

As a member of the Core Organising Team (COT), co-lead of the Technical Committee, and the primary lead for the Virtual Room, I had a front-row seat to this experiment. This is the story of how a small, dedicated group of volunteers brought a digital-first stage to life.

One of our core commitments on the COT for Wikimania 2026 was to meaningfully engage the global remote audience, not just broadcast physical sessions at them. The Technical Committee pitched several ideas to bridge the hybrid gap, and the Virtual Room was our boldest initiative.

Unlike standard track rooms, the Virtual Room had no physical space where people sat and watched. It existed entirely online, streamed through the live section of Eventyay and broadcast on the Wikimedia Foundation’s YouTube channel.
snippet: From 22 to 25 July 2026, Wikimania Paris featured a room that nobody could physically walk into.

title: How we measure contributions and recognise the most active contributors to Ukrainian Wikimedia sister projects
content:
Every year, Wikimedia Ukraine recognises some of the most active contributors to Ukrainian-language Wikimedia sister projects. To do this fairly, we look beyond simple edit counts: different projects involve very different types of work, so the indicators and tools we use depend on the nature of each project. This year, while determining winners for 2025, we also experimented with a new challenge — measuring contributions specifically to the Ukrainian-language layer of Wikidata.

For Ukraine, developing these projects has an additional significance. In the context of Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine, preserving, expanding and making Ukrainian-language knowledge accessible online is also part of strengthening the visibility and resilience of Ukrainian culture, history and language in the global information space.

title: Celebrating Community, Progress and Achievements at the Wikimedia Uganda Annual General Meeting 2026
content:
The Wikimedia Community User Group Uganda (WCUGU) held its Annual General Meeting (AGM) on Saturday, 5 September 2026, at Hotel Elianah, bringing together 77 participants, including volunteers, Board members, staff and partners. The AGM provided an opportunity for members to reflect on WCUGU’s work, discuss organisational development, share experiences and feedback, review financial performance, and identify priorities for the coming period, guided by four strategic objectives.

The AGM was attended by 77 participants, including Wikimedia volunteers, Board members, staff, partners and other stakeholders. Their participation created an opportunity to share experiences and perspectives on WCUGU’s development, strengthening community engagement. Media engagement also increased visibility, with Otage Stephen from Daily Monitor attending and the AGM shared on its social media platforms. The 7 September 2026 Daily Monitor edition also documented progress towards Runyankole Wikipedia going live. Links: Daily Monitor

title: Wikimedian Spotlight: Amina Alhassan (Tenacious Ntaawa), Growing Through Persistence and Community Support
content:
The Wikimedia movement grows because people dedicate their time, skills, and knowledge to making information accessible to everyone. Behind every contribution is a person with a story, and through our Wikimedian Spotlight series, we continue to recognize individuals whose efforts strengthen our community.

In this edition, the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group is pleased to spotlight Amina Alhassan, popularly known in the Wikimedia community as Tenacious Ntaawa, for her contributions to Wikimedia projects and her commitment to promoting Ghanaian languages online.

Amina’s Wikimedia journey started during her time at Tamale College of Education. She was introduced to Wikipedia by her senior, Achiri Bitamsimli, who brought the platform to her attention and helped her take her first steps into the Wikimedia movement.

Like many people who are introduced to Wikipedia for the first time, the beginning was not easy. Amina struggled to understand how the platform worked and how to make meaningful contributions. These difficulties sometimes discouraged her, leading her to stop contributing for a while.

title: “Beyond Editing”: a virtual gathering for Africa’s Users with Extended Rights
content:
Most readers never see this work. When a page is vandalised, someone reverts it. When an argument over sources gets heated, someone steps in. When a newcomer makes their first edit, someone checks it and, ideally, says, “Welcome.”

On many African-language wikis, that work rests with a small number of volunteers. They apply community policies, resolve disputes and support contributors, often across several languages and cultures at once, and often without many peers who do the same job.

This week, those volunteers get a space of their own. The African UwERs Virtual Pre-conference runs online on 6 and 7 November, ahead of WikiIndaba 2026. UwERs is shorthand for users with extended rights: administrators, patrollers and other functionaries. The organisers describe it as the first gathering of its kind.

The theme, “Beyond Editing”, is a reminder that writing articles is only one way to contribute. Keeping a wiki healthy, safe, and welcoming is work too. And it needs people.

The pre-conference is built for two groups. If you are a contributor wondering what else you could take on, it sets out to:

  • show you the range of roles and responsibilities available in Wikimedia communities

title: Small wikis in the age of AI: what breaks, what works, and what comes next
content:
On 21 July 2026, the day before Wikimania opened in Paris, I spoke at the Wiki AI pre-conference as an invited speaker. The session was not recorded, so this post is the public record of what was said, the evidence behind it, and what has happened since. For an overview of the whole day, see the organisers’ recap on Diff.

The talk was not about AI in general. It was about what AI does to the smallest wikis, including the ones I work on. I build and maintain tools that small and Indic-language communities rely on, so the question for me is practical: when an editor on a wiki with a handful of active contributors opens an AI assistant, what are they actually getting?

I opened with a question to the room: the same sentence, written in English and in Hindi, which one costs more to process?

The answer is Hindi, by a wide margin. Large language models do not read words; they read tokens. English text packs into few tokens. Devanagari, Bengali and Tamil text breaks into many more. For identical meaning, Hindi can take roughly two to three times as many tokens as English.

title: Digital Ethnography Jember Wins the 2026 Open Education Award for Open Practices
content:
Digital Ethnography Jember (Etno Digital Jember) has received a 2026 Open Education Award for Excellence from Open Education Global (OEGlobal). The winners were announced on September 2, 2026, with the initiative recognized in the Open Practices: How We Share category, which celebrates collaborative practices that expand access to education and open knowledge. From more than 200 nominations representing 49 countries, 16 initiatives were shortlisted as finalists in the Open Practices category. Digital Ethnography Jember was selected as one of four winners for its nomination, Digital Ethnography Jember: Open Cultural Heritage for Education.

Connecting Local Culture with Open Education

Digital Ethnography Jember is a community-based initiative that documents local cultural heritage and shares it through Wikimedia Commons, Wikidata, and Wikibooks. The initiative has produced more than 1,900 openly licensed media files covering traditions, traditional attire, museums, historical sites, local cuisine, and various aspects of Jember’s cultural heritage. These resources can be reused as learning materials, research references, and resources for developing open knowledge.
